items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $F\subset S^3$ be a nonempty compact smooth embedded surface with no closed components, possibly disconnected and nonorientable, and let $\alpha$ be a smoothly and properly embedded arc in $F$. Cut $F$ along a sufficiently small open rectangular neighborhood of $\alpha$ and round the resulting boundary corners inside $F$, obtaining $F'$. Then every component of $F'$ has nonempty boundary, the inclusion induces an injection $H_1(F';\mathbb Z)\hookrightarrow H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, and its full normal-transfer pairing is the pullback of that on $F$. In particular positive or negative definiteness is preserved by this cut.

Writing $c(F)$ for the number of connected components and $b_1(F)=\dim_{\mathbb Q}H_1(F;\mathbb Q)$, one has
$$b_1(F)-c(F)=b_1(F')+1-c(F').$$
More precisely, if the arc does not separate its component, then $c(F')=c(F)$ and $b_1(F')=b_1(F)-1$; if it separates its component, then $c(F')=c(F)+1$ and $b_1(F')=b_1(F)$. For a finite disjoint family of $m$ proper arcs, successive cuts retain the injection and pairing assertions and give $b_1(F)-c(F)=b_1(F')+m-c(F')$.

citations.quote:
Assume full AC. Let $F\subset S^3$ be a nonempty compact smooth embedded surface, possibly disconnected and nonorientable, every component of which has nonempty boundary. The ambient sphere has its standard orientation. The normal-transfer expression $B_F([a],[b])=\operatorname{lk}(a,\tau b)$ defines a symmetric integral bilinear pairing on the free finite-rank group $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, with rational extension. It restricts on each component to its normal-transfer pairing; for cycles $a,b$ on distinct components its value is $2\operatorname{lk}(a,b)$, which need not vanish.

Suppose an embedded product cylinder $W=[-1,1]\times D^2$ meets $F$ exactly in its two end disks, on distinct components. Replace those disks by the lateral annulus and round the seams to obtain $F'$. There is an integral basis in which $B_{F'}$ has matrix $G\oplus[0]$, where $G$ is the entire matrix of $B_F$, including its cross-component entries. Thus its signature is unchanged. The boundary link and its surface collar remain fixed, so $e(F)=-\sum_i\operatorname{lk}(K_i,K_i')$, computed from boundary normal push-offs, is unchanged as well.

A finite sequence of such tubes exists making $F$ connected. All intermediate surfaces still have the original boundary link and collar, no closed components, and finite smooth disk-and-band presentations on their components. The signature and $e$ are preserved throughout.

For an open cover $X=U\cup V$, the sequence
$$\cdots\to H_n(U\cap V;G)\to H_n(U;G)\oplus H_n(V;G)\to H_n(X;G)\xrightarrow{\delta}H_{n-1}(U\cap V;G)\to\cdots$$
is exact, with middle map $(u,v)\mapsto u+v$.

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be
$C^1$, and let $a\in U$.  If $Df(a)$ is invertible, then there are open sets
$V,W\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $a\in V\subseteq U$ and $f(a)\in W$ such that
$f|_V:V\to W$ is bijective.  Its inverse $g:W\to V$ is $C^1$, and

$$Dg(y)=Df(g(y))^{-1}\qquad(y\in W).$$

Thus $f$ is a local diffeomorphism at $a$.

Let $X$ be a smooth vector field on $M$. For each $p\in M$, let
$\gamma_p:I_p\to M$ be the maximal integral curve through $p$, and set

$$ \mathcal D:=\{(t,p)\in\mathbb R\times M:t\in I_p\}, \qquad \Phi(t,p):=\gamma_p(t). $$

Then $\mathcal D$ is open in $\mathbb R\times M$, each fibre $\mathcal D_p$ is
an interval containing $0$, the map $\Phi:\mathcal D\to M$ is smooth, and
$\Phi$ is the unique maximal local flow generated by $X$.

derivations.claim: The normal line of the arc in its surface is trivial, since the arc is an interval. Extend a transverse vector along its finitely many overlapping interval charts, changing its sign on an overlap if necessary; the interval has no cyclic compatibility condition. At its endpoints use proper boundary charts, so the transverse vector is tangent to the boundary. Extend this transverse vector to a smooth field near the arc, tangent to the boundary in its endpoint charts, using finitely many smooth chart cutoffs. Its short flow from [F4] and [F3] give a rectangular strip whose two end edges lie on $\partial F$. Removing a thinner open strip leaves a compact surface with four boundary corners; round them inward in the surface charts. This rounded subsurface is $F'$. A component that meets either cut edge has boundary there, and an untouched component has its original nonempty boundary. Thus no closed component is created. The affected original component has at most two resulting components: every component of its complement of the arc must meet one of the two connected side strips, or else it is open and closed in the original component. Rounding and shrinking the strip do not change this count.

Recover $F$ from $F'$ by attaching the removed rectangular strip along two intervals and undoing the small corner rounding. More precisely, a two-set relative-open cover consists of a small thickening $U$ of the cut subsurface and a thickened strip $V$; these retract onto $F'$ and a rectangle respectively, and their intersection retracts onto the two attaching intervals. Such retractions are the linear interval contractions in the strip and corner charts of step 1.1, fixed off those charts. Thus $H_1(U\cap V;\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_1(V;\mathbb Z)=0$. The sequence in [F2] gives an injection $H_1(F';\mathbb Z)\to H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ induced by inclusion, together with exact sequence $0\to H_1(F';\mathbb Z)\to H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\to\ker j\to0$, where $j:H_0(U\cap V;\mathbb Z)\to H_0(U;\mathbb Z)\oplus H_0(V;\mathbb Z)$.

If the two strip sides belong to one component of $F'$, their two degree-zero generators have the same image under $j$, with the common sign convention for the strip component. The kernel has rank one. If the sides belong to distinct components, their images have distinct $U$-coordinates and the kernel is zero. These are the only possibilities by step 1.1. In the first case $c(F')=c(F)$, and in the second case $c(F')=c(F)+1$. Finite ranks in [F1] and the exact sequence in step 2.1 give the two asserted first-Betti-number formulas. Rearranging either yields $b_1(F)-c(F)=b_1(F')+1-c(F')$.

Representatives for classes on $F'$ may be chosen in its interior by [F1], so they are also interior curves of $F$. Their sufficiently short normal pushes can be chosen identical on both surfaces, since the tangent planes agree on this subsurface. The two linking expressions defining their pairings therefore agree literally, even when two curves lie on different components of $F'$ or of $F$. This proves the pullback assertion. The injection in step 2.1 remains an injection over $\mathbb Q$: the groups are free by [F1], so clearing denominators verifies this directly. A nonzero rational class on $F'$ consequently maps to a nonzero class on $F$, and its quadratic value is that of this image. Either strict sign of definiteness is therefore retained.

For finitely many disjoint proper arcs choose their strips disjoint by compactness, with disjoint endpoint charts; proper disjointness includes their endpoints. After each cut the remaining arcs are still proper arcs on the resulting surface. Apply steps 1.1–3.2 successively. The homology injections and pullbacks compose, and definiteness is retained at every step. Summing the one-arc rank relation cancels the intermediate terms and gives $b_1(F)-c(F)=b_1(F')+m-c(F')$. The empty family has $m=0$ and is the identity operation. This proves the finite-family assertion with the same full scope.

boundaries.reason: A nonempty boundary link and spanning surfaces without closed components are assumed.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement allows zero first Betti number and zero signature; no inverse of the normal form is taken.
The Statement allows a one-component link and connected or disconnected surfaces satisfy the same argument.
The Statement uses the signature, which is the difference of positive and negative ranks; the proof does not require nonsingularity.
The Statement retains the same literal boundary link, with arbitrary component orientations.
The Statement explicitly assumes full AC, which is assumed and inherited through the cited linking and smooth construction suppliers.

axioms.use: Full AC is inherited from the full normal-transfer pairing on compact boundary surfaces. The relative strip charts, Mayer–Vietoris calculations and finite iteration use no additional choice principle.

risk_review.notes: Preserves full disconnected and nonorientable surface scope. All new prerequisite sources and their geometric constructions still require independent owner review.
